reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading is accurate: RPC custody columns bypass signature and inclusion proof verification (data_availability_checker.rs:240-267 performs only KZG verification via from_batch_with_scoring at L247-249, beacon_chain.rs:3716-3744 conditionally checks signatures but silently ignores failures). However, this is by design, NOT a vulnerability. The RPC parent check at beacon_chain.rs:3259-3265 ensures columns descend from fork-choice-approved blocks, meaning the block header was already fully validated (including signature) when the parent block was imported via gossip. RPC columns inherit authenticity from parent block validation. Per 01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json lines 642-657, property PROP-6a4369e9-asm-001 requires 'forall msg from P2P: processed(msg) => fully_validated(msg) == true', but RPC columns are NOT processed in isolation—they are components of blocks whose headers were validated at parent import time. The trust boundary differentiation between gossip (untrusted, first-contact) and RPC/sync (parent-validated, post-fork-choice) is an architectural security design. Spec-compliant per trust model.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: 01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json L642-657: 'P2P peers are untrusted; all P2P input must be fully validated before acceptance.' Applies to first-contact gossip, not RPC columns with fork-choice-validated parents.
